transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I'm here because I've been struggling with really severe mood swings for the past several months. I go through periods where I feel this intense, irritable energy, but then I crash into a deep depression and feel completely exhausted. It's just been this constant cycle of highs and lows that I can't seem to control.
Have you ever had hallucinations or strongly fixed beliefs that others said weren’t true during a time when your mood was otherwise normal, not during a high or a depression?
No, I've never experienced any hallucinations or strongly fixed beliefs when my mood was normal. Those kinds of things haven't happened to me outside of my highs and lows.

During your high-energy periods, have you ever felt so elevated or irritable that you needed much less sleep and it caused major problems, like being hospitalized or getting into serious trouble, for about a week or longer?

Yes, during those high-energy phases, which have lasted for about nine months, I feel incredibly elevated, irritable, and constantly driven to keep moving. I'm not really sure about needing less sleep specifically, and I haven't been hospitalized or gotten into serious trouble because of it.

During those high-energy periods, did your symptoms ever become severe enough to cause a major drop in your functioning, like being unable to work, needing emergency treatment, or doing clearly risky things that were very out of character?

I don't really recall doing anything extremely risky or needing emergency treatment when I was like that. I'm not sure if it caused a major drop in my daily functioning, but I don't think it got to that extreme point.
During those high-energy periods, did you ever have hallucinations or beliefs that others said were clearly untrue, even if you weren’t hospitalized?
No, I've never experienced anything like that. Even when my energy was really high and I was feeling irritable, I didn't have any hallucinations or beliefs that weren't true.
During those high-energy periods, were there times when you slept much less than usual and still felt rested and full of energy the next day?
To be honest, I'm not really sure about my sleep patterns during those high-energy times. I haven't noticed sleeping less while still feeling rested.
Were those high-energy feelings present nearly every day for most of those nine months, or did they come in shorter episodes with clear starts and stops?

Yes, those high-energy feelings and the constant urge to keep moving were present nearly every day for that entire nine-month period. It didn't really come in short, separate episodes with clear breaks; it was just a continuous, ongoing state for me.

During the times you crashed into depression, did you have at least two weeks of feeling down or losing interest most of the day nearly every day, along with symptoms like sleep or appetite changes, low energy, guilt, poor concentration, or thoughts of death?

Yes, those crashes lasted much longer than two weeks, actually going on for about 11 months. I felt persistently down, sad, empty, and completely numb emotionally. On top of that, I had an overwhelming loss of energy and felt extreme physical and mental fatigue every single day.
Have you felt depressed most of the time for at least two years, without being free of symptoms for more than two months at a time?
No, I wouldn't say it has been going on for two years. While I have been feeling very depressed and down, these feelings have actually lasted for about 11 months.

During that nine-month high-energy period, did you also have things like unusually fast thoughts or speech, feeling more confident than usual, being more talkative, or getting unusually distracted or goal-driven?

I don't really recall having fast thoughts, feeling unusually confident, or being more talkative during that time. However, I definitely had an overwhelming amount of energy and just couldn't seem to sit still.

Psychotic disorders remain unlikely because the patient denies hallucinations or delusions outside mood episodes and also during the high-energy state.

opening_question.question: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

final_diagnosis.reason: The clearest syndrome established is a major depressive episode lasting about 11 months, with persistent depressed mood, emotional numbness, and marked low energy/fatigue causing significant distress. Bipolar II Disorder was considered because of prolonged irritability/high energy, but the interview did not confirm distinct hypomanic episodes with the required cluster of hypomanic symptoms; instead, the high-energy state was continuous for months without clear episodic onset/offset and without decreased need for sleep, increased talkativeness, grandiosity, racing thoughts, or risky behavior. ADHD hyperactive/impulsive presentation is less likely because the symptoms were described as a recent mood-linked change over months rather than a longstanding childhood-onset neurodevelopmental pattern.
